issues.body:
Automatic per-paragraph language identification for proofing routing with Google CLD3. GlotLID is out of scope.

## What

- **New MIT package `packages/quds_language_id`**
  - **Runtime:** CrispASR's `crisp_lid/src/lid_cld3.{h,cpp}` at `19d86f9b` (the last `crisp_lid` change, an ancestor of `origin/main`), compiled unchanged. No CrispASR change was needed.
  - **No ggml:** `lid_cld3.cpp` computes in plain C++ and uses ggml/gguf only to load weights. `native/shim/` and `native/src/gguf_shim.cpp` provide those calls over a bounded GGUF v2/v3 reader (F32/F16 only). The fastText backend and `text_lid_dispatch` are not compiled.
  - **Workers:** an FFI isolate natively and a module Web Worker on the web (Emscripten). `tool/build.py` admits only the pinned files (length and SHA-256), checks them against the licence manifest and writes receipts. The build is reproducible: two builds gave identical hashes.
  - **Model:** `cld3-f16.gguf` (439,712 bytes, Apache-2.0), from `cstr/cld3-GGUF@56e8a57d`, is **bundled as an asset** and pinned by SHA-256. A tampered model is never opened.
  - **API:** `Cld3LanguageIdentifier.detect(text)` / `detectBatch(texts)` return the top-5 `LanguageGuess(language, confidence)`. CLD3 labels map to BCP-47 (`iw`→`he`, `jw`→`jv`, `in`→`id`, `ji`→`yi`; `*-Latn` kept).
- **Engine** (`language_identification.dart`, testable through `LanguageIdentifier`, like `ArabicMorphology`):
  - script segmentation, `LanguageDetectionPolicy`, `ParagraphLanguageDetector` (batched, LRU-cached) and `resolveDetectedLanguage`;
  - `wordRunLanguageSlot`, which defines "default".
- **Editor:**
  - `WordProofingSession.configureLanguageDetection` and `automaticLanguageDetection`. A pass detects uncached paragraphs in one batch, then routes each script segment.
  - `WordTextProofingTarget.scriptLanguages` and `detectedLanguages`.
  - `WordEditorController.applyDetectedTextProofingLanguages`: `w:val` for Latin segments, `w:bidi` for Arabic/Hebrew segments, one undo step.
  - Review pane: "Latin text: English · Arabic text: English", "Detected: Latin text: German · Arabic text: Arabic" and **Apply detected language**.
- **Studio:**
  - a bundled-model host, native and web;
  - the setting **Detect language automatically**, on by default;
  - CLD3 (Apache-2.0) and CrispASR (MIT) notices on the licence page.
- **Docs:** a `docs/PROOFING.md` section (policy, evaluation, cost, licence), the receipt `docs/evidence/language-id-ud-r2.14.json` and the package README.

## Policy and thresholds

1. **Script first.** Each paragraph is split into Unicode script runs; neutral characters join the preceding run. Each run gets its own language.
2. **Arabic script** is `ar` unless CLD3 says fa/ur/ps/ku/sd/ug with p ≥ 0.95 on ≥ 20 letters. **Hebrew script** is `he` unless it says `yi` under the same condition.
3. **Latin and other scripts:** CLD3's top language applies only with **≥ 20 letters**, **p ≥ 0.95**, and a language of that script.
4. **Precedence:**
   - An explicit run/paragraph language wins.
   - A **default** yields to the detection. Default means a missing `w:lang` slot, or a value equal to the `w:docDefaults` language.
   - The default tag is kept when the detection has the same primary subtag (de-CH stays de-CH).
   - The default is kept when CLD3 still gives it p ≥ 0.01 in its top 5.
5. Detection never edits the document. Only the explicit Apply action does, and it is undoable.

## Evaluation (UD r2.14 test `# text`)

| Language | Sentences | CLD3 top-1 | <20 | 20–50 | >50 | Policy detects | Wrong overrides |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| en EWT | 2036 | 70.6% | 22.4% | 73.5% | 93.6% | 56.1% | 13 (0.64%) |
| de GSD | 977 | 93.4% | 48.4% | 79.1% | 99.3% | 87.2% | 5 (0.51%) |
| fr GSD | 416 | 97.4% | 33.3% | 88.0% | 99.7% | 93.8% | 0 |
| ar PUD | 1000 | 99.6% | 85.7% | 97.4% | 100% | 100% | 0 |
| he HTB | 491 | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 0 |
| la Perseus+PROIEL | 2199 | 84.2% | 43.1% | 75.2% | 97.3% | 67.8% | 21 (0.95%) |
| es GSD | 426 | 96.9% | 100% | 84.8% | 98.4% | 91.1% | 1 (0.23%) |
| it ISDT | 482 | 93.4% | 40.0% | 81.5% | 98.3% | 87.6% | 6 (1.24%) |

- **Overall:** 46 of 8,027 sentences (0.57%) would be wrongly overridden. 72.7% switch correctly when another same-script language is the default.
- **Top confusions:** la→fr 60, la→it 45, en→el-Latn 34, en→fr 30, en→zu 27, en→lb 24, la→pt 22, de→lb 13, it→co 11. The English errors are mostly signatures, URLs and names in EWT.
- **Mixed-script paragraphs (200 each):** the Arabic/Hebrew segment is right in 1000 of 1000. The Latin segment is right/wrong/abstained in de+ar 176/2/22, en+ar 150/3/47, fr+he 187/0/13, en+he 150/3/47, la+ar 119/0/81.

## Cost

These figures come from an Apple M1 under heavy load from other agents.

- **Latency per paragraph:**
  - Native: AOT Dart, through the policy and the isolate, one request per paragraph. Mean 0.17–0.32 ms, p95 0.38–0.74 ms.
  - Web: headless Chrome 157, through the dart2js transport and the worker. Mean 0.37 ms, p95 0.7 ms; the worker and model open in 0.38 s.
- **Size added:**
  - the model, 439,712 bytes;
  - the macOS arm64 dylib, 103,272 bytes;
  - wasm 49,233, mjs 9,604 and worker 3,775 bytes.
- **Memory:**
  - Native: +3.3 MB RSS after load.
  - Web: a 16 MB initial Wasm heap.

## Tests

Validated locally; CI was skipped (`[skip ci]`).

- **`quds_language_id`:** 10 pass (6 unit + 4 native with the real dylib and model).
  - Node worker smoke: 5 protocol checks.
  - Headless Chrome smoke of the dart2js transport and worker: passed.
  - dart2js compile check: passed.
- **Engine `test/proofing/`:** 1697 pass, including 20 new policy tests with a fake detector.
- **`quds_arabic_morph`:** 10 pass, 15 skipped. The skips are the existing real-backend gates; the e2e path is unchanged.
- **Editor:** 1945 pass, 1 skipped, 10 fail. This includes 7 new tests (routing, setting, per-script target, apply/undo/DOCX, review-pane widget).
  - The 10 failures are the same set on clean `origin/main`: 8 in `embed_test.dart`, 1 in `word_bookmark_history_test.dart`, and `office_story_golden_test.dart`, which also fails on main on this host.
- **Studio example:** 341 pass, 3 skipped, 0 fail. This includes 4 new tests (asset pin, missing-library host, settings switch with dialog display and Apply, licence page).

## Remaining

- Upstream CLD3 snippet selection (`ScriptScanner`, `CheapSqueeze`) and full Unicode lowercasing are simplified in the CrispASR port. Accuracy on short text is CLD3's own limit. GlotLID remains out of scope.
- Packaging the native library and web worker into release app bundles uses `build.py --install-*`, as for the morphology backend; no binaries are committed.
- Draft (reply) checks still use the document language.
- The setting is per session and not persisted, like the other Studio view settings.

issues.body:
## Why

On-premises Exchange installations need a direct EWS mail path without requiring IMAP/SMTP services or a Microsoft 365 account. This adds a shared native EWS provider and a usable Exchange Server entry in Office Studio.

## What changes

- Add `MailProviderKind.ews` and `MailEwsProvider`, implementing both existing mail and submission ports. Opaque ItemIds remain case-sensitive; existing store/coordinator contracts handle page-and-cursor commits.
- Default to NTLMv2 over verified HTTPS, including MIC and TLS channel binding. Authenticate with body-free HEAD requests and retain the same connection for SOAP. Basic is explicit; hosts may supply bearer tokens. Credentials never follow redirects, and there is no public certificate bypass.
- Implement paged mail folders and headers, `SyncFolderItems`, bounded MIME reading, read/flag changes, move, and move-to-Deleted-Items. Fetch current ChangeKeys before conditional writes and require observed confirmation. Only explicit invalid SyncState errors reset synchronization.
- Send with `CreateItem/SendAndSaveCopy`, validating MIME against the frozen recipient envelope and preserving hidden recipients. A possibly accepted submission becomes uncertain and is never automatically replayed.
- Add a native, session-only Studio view with manual endpoint settings, NTLMv2 default, explicit Basic, folder/message browsing, existing Word composer and reply/forward, mutation controls, and English/German/Arabic feedback.
- Add a read-only endpoint probe, deployment documentation, regression evidence, and mail/Studio CI jobs. XML and Pointy Castle become direct transport dependencies without changing any locked version or archive hash.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Core / MIME / store / transport VM suites | 54 + 32 + 118 + 227 = **431 passed** |
| JavaScript/Node EWS and existing IMAP boundary | **11 passed** |
| Studio mail regression across 11 files | **157 passed**, including all 15 new EWS widget cases |
| Independent pyspnego NTLMv2 acceptor | **5 expected outcomes**, including rejected channel-binding and MIC tampering |
| Relevant Dart/Flutter analysis and diff checks | **Clean** |

Review found and fixed a Load More path that could bypass the required refresh after an unconfirmed mutation. Final widget results include that correction. The published Git tree matches the locally tested tree: `bfe1bce1545657b7deacadc63c30e99f9fb82880`.

## Qualification boundary

No live Exchange endpoint or credentials were supplied. Actual Exchange/IIS/Extended Protection policy and installed-platform acceptance remain to be checked using the probe and a disposable test mailbox. These are local results; no hosted CI outcome or packaged application build is asserted.

Studio credentials, downloaded mail and drafts are kept only for the foreground session. The shared provider supports host-owned vault/repository ports, while durable Studio outbox integration remains separate. Autodiscover, Kerberos, OAuth acquisition, Calendar/Contacts, public/archive folders and full delegation are outside this change.

- [Setup and API guide](https://github.com/CrispStrobe/quds_office_suite/blob/feat/ews-on-premises/docs/roadmaps/mail/exchange-ews.md)
- [Source-bound validation record](https://github.com/CrispStrobe/quds_office_suite/blob/feat/ews-on-premises/docs/validation/mail-ews-20261119/README.md)

issues.body:
## Summary

Switches `quds_arabic_morph` to the binary proofing database and CrispEmbed's compact ABI, from CrispStrobe/CrispEmbed#255 (commit `0ed76631`, ABI 2).

- **Data:** the catalog and Studio now use `camelMorphMsaProofingBin` (`cstr/camel-morph-msa-v1.0@d5364e04…/proofing-bin`, 11.6 MB instead of 74.5 MB). It is the noprob database, memory-mapped, reduced to the 24 features the rules and lemma identity use. Analyses and those values are exact against camel_tools; see CrispEmbed's `docs/validation/camel-morph-binary-20261119`.
- **Migration:** the Studio native host calls `MorphInstaller.removeOtherBundles` on refresh, so the old noprob install is removed and the user downloads the new bundle once.
- **Transport:** the FFI isolate and the Web Worker call the batched `crispembed_ar_morph_analyze_compact`, with no JSON. Each batch comes back as one transferred buffer.
- **Cache:** `CompactAnalysisDecoder` keeps compact per-word records (about 1–2 KB) whose maps read features lazily and intern decoded values. Repeated projected analyses are dropped.
- **Build:** `tool/build.py` is repinned (26 files), and the licence bundle, data NOTICE and Studio licence assets are refreshed. Wasm `INITIAL_MEMORY` is now 16 MB.
- **Tools:** new `tool/pud_rule_findings.dart`; `pud_benchmark`, `web_smoke` and `browser_smoke` are updated.

## Measurements

Apple M1 on a shared machine (load 4–26). Corpus: the 1,000 UD Arabic-PUD sentences, 7,419 distinct words.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native load (Dart API) | 1.5–2.5 s | 0.16–0.26 s |
| Native RSS after load | 230–250 MB | 30 MB (the process starts at 18 MB) |
| Native RSS with all words analyzed | 373–415 MB | 90–100 MB (Dart old space about 40 MB, was 180 MB) |
| Native words/s through Dart | 709–921 (interleaved median 429) | 1,750–2,955 (interleaved median 1,802) |
| Node Wasm | 1.4 s load, 1,750 words/s, 320 MB heap | 0.13 s, 3,290 words/s, 16–19 MB heap |
| Chrome Wasm (Dart web transport) | 1.4 s, 916–948 words/s, 320 MB worker heap, 203 MB page heap | 0.15 s, 3,493–3,523 words/s, 16–19 MB worker heap, 41 MB page heap |

The rules report the same 673 findings on all 1,000 PUD sentences in three setups: the old backend (JSON, noprob), the new backend with proofing-bin, and the new backend with noprob.

## Tests (local)

All run with the real library and the real proofing-bin bundle:

- `quds_arabic_morph`: 29 tests pass, including the rules e2e test and the live Hugging Face download.
- Studio: the morph setup, morph native, Hunspell setup and Arabic proofing native tests pass.
- Engine: `test/proofing` passes, 1,677 tests.

`origin/main` is merged.
